title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Design, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview:

Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) through H1 2027. It is intended for engineering, product, GTM, and support teams to align on scope, acceptance criteria, launch plan, and go-to-market messaging.

Context and problem statement
-----------------------------
Customers need a single, consistent inference runtime that:
- Delivers predictable latency and throughput across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Provides cost controls, model routing, and fallbacks to ensure reliability under constrained capacity.
- Enables platform teams to standardize instrumentation, SLOs, and rollout patterns.

This product expands Redwood's Unified Inference surface by formalizing the API, rollout patterns, pricing, and operational guardrails required for enterprise adoption.

Goals & Non-goals
------------------
Goals (success criteria):
1. Provide a single API surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with consistent semantics across deployment modes.
2. Achieve 95th-percentile latency SLOs for common request types (see SLO table) in Hosted and Dedicated tiers at launch.
3. Launch model routing and cost-aware fallback policies that reduce error rate during capacity events by >= 70% versus no-fallback baseline.
4. Introduce pricing tiers and reserve capacity packaging that support self-serve up to $50k/month ARR and sales-assisted contracts beyond.
5. Provide observability dashboards (per-route cost, latency, token breakdown, error classification) and rollout controls (canary, A/B, auto-fallback) in Redwood Console.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not include development of new model architectures or model training pipelines.
- Deep custom integrations for individual regulated customers (handled as Professional Services).

-----------------------------

Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)
----------------------------------
MUST (minimum viable):
1. API parity: Same REST/SDK endpoints for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
2. SLOs:
   - Generation (short form <=128 tokens): P50 < 30ms, P95 < 120ms (hosted), P95 < 150ms (dedicated baseline).
   - Chat (multi-turn reuse): P95 end-to-end < 250ms for cached KV-hit paths.
   - Embeddings: P95 < 80ms for single-document embedding.
3. Model routing: Policy engine to route requests by latency budget, cost budget, and region with automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants.
4. Observability: Per-route token-level cost, latency percentiles, error rates, and sampling for outputs tied to prompt sets.
5. Rollouts: Canary/A-B with automatic rollback on defined error/latency thresholds; configurable by model/version/route.
6. Security: TLS in-transit, KMS integration for private deployments, RBAC mapping to account/route.
7. Documentation: Quickstarts, SDK examples, migration guide for customers moving from existing APIs.

SHOULD (important but not blocking):
1. Auto-batching suggestions (Redwood Optimize integration) for common route patterns.
2. Prefix/KV caching with TTLs configurable per route.
3. Built-in eval hooks for regression detection (integration with applied-ml-and-evals).

MAY (nice-to-have):
1. Cost prediction for scheduled workloads.
2. Per-tenant quantization profiles offered as recommendation.

Acceptance criteria (examples)
------------------------------
- Integration tests show API parity across modes with < 1% behavior divergence for canonical calls.
- Performance benchmarks for targeted model families (Llama2-13B, Falcon-40B) meet SLOs in staged capacity.
- Console dashboards show per-route cost and latency within 1 hour of ingestion.
- Canary rollout was exercised in staging and automatic rollback triggered correctly for a fault injection.

Design & Architecture (high level)
----------------------------------
1) Runtime & kernel selection
- Serving runtime selects optimized kernels based on model family, sequence length distribution, and device capacity. Kernel selection profile stored as simple JSON list per model-version (see Appendix A example).

2) Smart routing policy engine
- Policy inputs: latency budget, cost tier, geographic region, model capability tag, tenant preference.
- Decision graph: route -> capacity check -> model variant selection -> fallback path.

3) Caching and batching
- Automatic prefix caching with configurable TTL per route.
- Continuous batching with latency-budget aware thresholds.

4) Observability hooks
- Token-level tracing with sampling; per-request metadata emitted to tracing pipeline with route/model tags.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO, cost, p99 latency, errors by class.

Design tradeoffs and rationale
-----------------------------
- Prioritize deterministic API semantics across environments to reduce customer migration cost.
- Conservative default SLOs balance cost and latency for early adopters; customers can tighten SLOs in Dedicated with capacity reservations.
- Fallbacks favor compatibility (quantized variants) over model downgrades that change output semantics.

Design Spec — Key data tables and configs
----------------------------------------
Model catalog (example rows):
| model_id | family | variant | quantized | recommended_deploy | notes |
|----------|--------|---------|-----------|--------------------|-------|
| redwood/llama2-13b | Llama2 | v1.2 | int8 | hosted,dedicated,private | baseline release |
| redwood/falcon-40b | Falcon | v3.0 | int8 | dedicated,private | long-context optimized |

Route configuration example (YAML):
- route: /v1/generate/text
  model: redwood/llama2-13b:v1.2
  latency_budget_ms: 120
  fallback: [redwood/llama2-13b:int8, redwood/llama2-7b:v1.0]
  cache_ttl_sec: 30
  observability: { sampling_rate: 0.01 }

Roadmap & themes (Q1–Q2 2027)
-----------------------------
Themes by quarter (high level):
- Q1 2027: Platform-parity & SLO stabilization — complete API parity, baseline SLOs, rollout control prototypes.
- Q2 2027: Cost controls & Optimize integration — auto-batching suggestions, prefix caching, first set of quantization recommendations.
- H2 2027: Enterprise readiness & Private GA — KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging improvements, compliance evidence.

Milestones & timeline (targets)
- 2027-01-15: Internal alpha — API parity validated in staging.
- 2027-02-28: Private beta — selected customers on Dedicated and Private.
- 2027-03-15: Documentation and public pricing proposal (this doc).
- 2027-04-30: Hosted GA for Unified Inference v1 (self-serve).
- 2027-06-30: Dedicated GA + Redwood Optimize vX cost controls.

Pricing & packaging guidance
----------------------------
High-level packaging:
- Self-serve Hosted Tiers: Free trial credit; Pay-as-you-go (per-token generation & embeddings), with standard and pro throughput plans.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity commitments (bronze/silver/gold) with minimum 3-month terms.
- Private: tiered platform fee + optional professional services.

Suggested pricing matrix (example):
| Tier | Billing model | SLA | Target customer | Notes |
|------|---------------|-----|-----------------|-------|
| Free | Credit-based | none | Developers, quickstarts | 10k tokens free/mo trial |
| Standard | PAYG per-token | best-effort | Startups, app developers | competitive per-token rate |
| Pro | PAYG + throughput | 99.9% | Growing companies | discounts at 100k+ monthly tokens |
| Dedicated Bronze | Monthly reserved GPU hours | 99.95% | Mid-market | baseline capacity |
| Dedicated Gold | Annual reserved capacity + support | 99.99% | Enterprise | includes priority on-call & migration support |

Pricing considerations & guardrails:
- Model variants (quantized) should have separate price multipliers (e.g., int8 = -25% cost).
- Embeddings priced per 1k vectors with tiered discounts.
- Burst capacity pricing for Dedicated to cover short spikes.

Go-to-market and launch checklist
--------------------------------
Pre-launch (internal):
1. Finalize API contract and SDKs (Python, JS).
2. Run performance validation matrix across model families and hardware.
3. Prepare console dashboards and rollout controls.
4. Prepare migration guides and sample prompts.

Launch (external):
1. Publish docs, quickstarts, and pricing page.
2. Engage early beta customers with onboarding playbook.
3. Release marketing collateral and benchmark comparisons.

Post-launch:
1. Monitor SLOs and error budgets (eng-sre).
2. Iterate on pricing tiers based on usage patterns.

Release Notes (snapshot — 2027-03-15)
-------------------------------------
This release bundles the following artifacts for public/internal release:
- API spec: v1.0-unified (generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) — documented and SDKed.
- Console: rollout control beta and per-route cost dashboard.
- Runtime: kernel-selection improvements for Llama2-13B and Falcon-40B; fallback policy engine prototype.
- Docs: migration guide, quickstarts, and PRD (this doc).

Known limitations and follow-ups
------------------------------
- Some model families (very large context models) will not meet production SLOs on smallest Dedicated plans; documented in model catalog.
- Private deployments require customer network readiness checklist (see Appendix B).
- Observability ingestion latency currently targeted at < 1 hour; ops effort scheduled to reduce to < 15 minutes in Q2.

Operational runbooks & escalation
--------------------------------
- Runbooks live in eng-platform/runbooks/unified-inference-runbook.md (link).
- On-call escalation: S1 (model-serving down), S2 (SLO violation persistent > 30m), S3 (degraded performance). Contacts: oncall page.

Appendix A — Example kernel-profile JSON (textified)
{
  "model_id": "redwood/llama2-13b:v1.2",
  "kernels": ["fused_attention_v2","quant_matmul_int8"],
  "sequence_length_breakpoints": [128,512,2048]
}

Appendix B — Private deployment readiness checklist
1. VPC peering and DNS resolution validated.
2. KMS/HSM keys provisioned and accessible.
3. Minimum GPU node capacity validated (per customer sizing).
4. Audit logging sink configured (S3/Cloud Storage).
